description: Starts broad (machine learning basics), then narrows into attention and transformers, so renames and re-parenting become worthwhile.

prompts.text: What's the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
Why do we need a separate test set if we already have a validation set?
What is overfitting and how can I tell it's happening from the loss curves?
Can you explain the bias-variance tradeoff with a simple example?
How does k-fold cross-validation work?
Is accuracy a bad metric for imbalanced classes? What should I use instead?
Why does L1 regularization give sparse weights but L2 doesn't?
What problem do recurrent neural networks solve that feedforward ones don't?
Why do LSTMs have gates? What's the forget gate for?
What's the problem with RNNs on long sentences?
What is attention in seq2seq models? The decoder 'looks at' the encoder states?
In self-attention, what are queries, keys and values? Where do they come from?
Why do we divide by sqrt(d_k) in scaled dot-product attention?
How does the transformer know the word order if attention is permutation invariant?
Why sinusoidal positional encodings instead of just learning position embeddings?
What's the point of multi-head attention? Isn't one head enough?
I tried to compute attention weights by hand for 3 tokens: softmax of QK^T. Is each row supposed to sum to 1?
How does the causal mask work in the decoder?
Is the transformer encoder the same as BERT?
How do the heads get combined after multi-head attention, just concatenation?
Why is attention O(n^2) in sequence length? Is that why context windows are limited?
What's the difference between self-attention and cross-attention in the decoder?
Do I add or concatenate the positional encoding to the token embedding?
What does the padding mask do, and how is it different from the causal mask?
Can you quiz me on the transformer architecture? I want to check I understand the whole forward pass.
